material_definitions: The electrical properties and the crystal structure were investigated for the ceramic electrolytes based on LiHf2(PO4)3.
The conductivity enhanced by the Li2O addition with LiHf2(PO4)3 system and by the increase of x for Li(1+x)M(x)Hf(2-x)(PO4)3 (M = Cr, Fe, Sc, In, Lu or Y) systems.
The P21/n monoclinic phase transformed to NASICON-type R3c rhombohedral phase at above 1173 K.
The material series is LiHf2(PO4)3+yLi2O.
Li2O addition acts as a flux to achieve high-density samples.
Sintering above 1293 K induces a phase transition from the monoclinic phase (P21/n) to the highly conductive NASICON-type rhombohedral phase (R3c).
The conductivity enhancement is attributed to both the phase formation and decreased porosity.
This specific sample achieved maximum total conductivity when sintered at 1298 K.
The materials are ceramic electrolytes based on LiHf2(PO4)3, forming the NASICON-type R3c structure.
The series is Li(1+x)M(x)Hf(2-x)(PO4)3 where M=Cr, Fe, Sc, In, Lu, or Y.
Samples were sintered above 1293 K to obtain high density and maximum conductivity.
The conductivity enhancement is due to high densification and decreased activation energy at the grain boundary.
measurements.source_caption: The total conductivity at 298 K for Lit +xMxHf2\_x(PO4)3 M=Cr (@);Fe (A);Sc (V);In (ll);Lu (0) orY (e).
warnings: Raw conductivity unit was written as 'S.cm-4' in one instance, but 'S.cm-1' in the summarizing conclusion; S.cm-1 was used as it is chemically plausible.

material_definitions: This conductivity value serves as a reference point for comparison with LiHf2(PO4)3 systems.
The activation energy for the bulk component of this system is reported as 0.30 eV.
warnings: Value is cited from external references [10, 11].
Temperature (298 K) is inferred based on comparison with the preceding measurement in the text.
